samples.question: The six framed tiles are a key: the two small dots on a tile are a pair of colors, in no particular order, and the big square on that tile is the color that pair produces. Seven colored disks sit in a ring and one is circled in black. In one round every disk is replaced at the same moment: a disk's new color is the square on the tile whose two dots match the colors of the two disks next to it in the ring, and its own color does not matter. Because all seven change together, always read neighbors as they were before the round, never as you have just rewritten them. Carry out five rounds. What color is the circled disk then? Answer amber, crimson, or teal.
